column1: # leak-patterns.tsv — the denylist the leak gate applies to this repo.
# Format: NAME<TAB>EXTENDED_REGEX   ('#' comments and blank lines ignored). PCRE, so inline
# flags like (?i) work.
# VALUE-FREE BY DESIGN. This file is public, so it must not list the identifiers it exists to
# catch — a denylist that names your Telegram chat id has itself leaked it. The patterns below
# describe the SHAPE of identifying data instead. Shape patterns are also strictly stronger:
# they catch a second host, account or key that a value list never knew about.
# Only the entries marked REPLACE need editing.
# They are INERT until you do: a pattern still containing `<YOUR_...>` matches that literal
# placeholder text and nothing else, so the check it names catches nothing. leak-scan.sh
# counts them and says so in its verdict, so a PASS is never read as coverage that does
# not exist.
# NOTE: these four are intentionally left as <YOUR_...> in the PUBLIC template — this file
# ships to other agents who fork this kit. Each adopter replaces them with their own values
# (or deletes the rows they do not want). Until then the named checks are INERT and
# leak-scan.sh says so in every verdict — that warning is the design working, not a bug.
identity-name
owner-handle
repo-name
profile-path
# Deliberately NOT included: a generic IPv4 pattern (it matches version strings such as
# 6.30.5.105) and a generic *.sqlite pattern (not identifying on its own). A shape pattern has
# to be both identifying AND precise — a noisy gate gets switched off, which is worse than none.
telegram-id
ssh-key
absolute-home
local-endpoint
contact-email
health-dir
# --- personal measurements: a marker next to a number, or a number with a body unit ------
health-marker
health-unit
